abstract UVM environment
build_phase (top → down)       connect_phase (bottom → up)
<env> creates <agent>, <checker>   <producer>.ap ──connect──► <subscriber>.analysis_export
<agent> creates <driver>, <monitor>   ports meet after every component exists

The environment (uvm_env) is the composition root for a testbench. This lesson's one idea is the two-step assembly: first create the hierarchy, then connect the ports. Keeping those steps separate lets the same agent plug into different checkers.

Its reusable shape is:

class <name> extends uvm_env;
  <agent_type> agent;
  function void build_phase(uvm_phase phase);
    agent = <agent_type>::type_id::create("agent", this);
  endfunction
  function void connect_phase(uvm_phase phase);
    agent.monitor.ap.connect(<subscriber>.analysis_export);
  endfunction
endclass

Two phases do the work:

  • build_phase — creates child components top-down with type_id::create("name", this)
  • connect_phase — wires TLM ports between components bottom-up
  mem_env
  ├─ mem_agent
  │    ├─ uvm_sequencer
  │    ├─ mem_driver  ──► DUT (sram)
  │    └─ mem_monitor ◄── DUT (sram)
  │         └─ ap (analysis_port)
  │              ├──► mem_scoreboard.analysis_export
  │              └──► mem_coverage.analysis_export
  ├─ mem_scoreboard
  └─ mem_coverage

In this SRAM environment, the monitor's ap feeds both the scoreboard and the coverage collector. Each subscriber gets one connect() call, with no changes to the monitor. Open mem_env.sv and complete both phases:

  • In build_phase: create agent, scbd, and cov using type_id::create
  • In connect_phase: connect the monitor's analysis port to both the scoreboard and coverage exports

The this argument in create("name", this) sets the UVM hierarchy parent. This determines the component's path in the tree, which scopes config_db lookups and reporting output.
